central_thesis: Preply moved its homepage from aspirational lifestyle positioning — 'Make the world your comfort zone', 'Prepare to speak confidently' — to outcome-first messaging anchored in speed and scale proof, suggesting the company began addressing visitors who are already comparing tutors rather than still imagining the benefit of language learning.
old_positioning_frame: Language learning as personal transformation and confidence — identity-driven, aspirational, lifestyle framing.
new_positioning_frame: Fast, matched-tutor progress with visible scale proof — efficiency-driven, with enterprise signal ('Book a demo') alongside the individual learner path.
buyer_shift: Self-motivated learners seeking confidence and life transformation → outcome-focused learners comparing providers on speed and tutor fit; plus a visible B2B/team-learning audience ('Book a demo').
funnel_shift: Awareness-stage visitors who need to be convinced language learning will help them → solution-aware visitors who know they want a tutor and are evaluating which platform delivers it fastest.

main_evidence.old: Prepare to speak confidently with the best online tutors
main_evidence.new: Learn faster with your best language tutor.
main_evidence.meaning: The shift from 'speak confidently' to 'Learn faster' suggests a move toward solution-aware buyers who are past the aspiration stage. 'Your best tutor' (possessive, singular) is consistent with addressing a visitor who already knows they want a tutor, not someone still exploring the category.

main_evidence.old: Make the world your comfort zone | Focus on the skills you need | Request a private tutor
main_evidence.meaning: Removing 'Make the world your comfort zone' is consistent with dropping identity and lifestyle framing in favor of functional value. 'Request a private tutor' (request = supply-constrained, high-friction) suggests a move toward self-serve browsing rather than mediated matching.

A 'Book a demo' CTA on a consumer tutoring homepage is the strongest enterprise-motion signal in the evidence. It suggests Preply is serving or testing team and corporate language learning alongside the individual learner segment — a meaningful expansion of audience scope.

main_evidence.old: Chinese tutors | Arabic tutors | Japanese tutors | Polish tutors | Dutch tutors
main_evidence.new: Chinese tutors 5,253 teachers | Arabic tutors 3,651 teachers | Japanese tutors 2,902 teachers | Polish tutors 362 teachers | Dutch tutors 234 teachers
main_evidence.meaning: Adding explicit tutor counts to language category links is consistent with shifting from awareness-stage messaging to solution-aware proof. A visitor who is comparing providers benefits from seeing scale; a visitor who is still learning the category is unlikely to need it.

copy_this_if: Your brand name already appears in searches without requiring a category explanation — visitors arrive knowing what you do, and need you to show them why you are the right provider, not what the category is.
do_not_copy_this_if: Your audience is still learning that their problem has a solution. Efficiency copy ('learn faster', 'ship faster') does not land with someone who has not yet decided to solve the problem at all.
